hero-subtext: I study how fluids, plasmas and fields behave in microgravity — and build the small spacecraft that carry those questions into orbit.
about-lead: I'm an Aerospace Engineering undergraduate at the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology, Thiruvananthapuram — currently in my third year.
about-body: My research interests sit at the intersection of interfacial fluid dynamics in microgravity conditions, magnetohydrodynamics for space applications, and computational plasma physics. Alongside this, I work on the development of CubeSats under the Small Spacecraft Systems and Payload Centre (SSPACE), IIST, where I'm involved in the thermal subsystem.

research.title: “Ultrasound-induced wetting dynamics of a molten metallic droplet”
research.venue: International Conference on Interfacial Phenomena in Droplets
research.abstract: The spreading of a liquid droplet results from the combined effect of capillary forces and viscous resistance. Under ultrasonic excitation, additional acoustic forcing can drive liquid motion and significantly alter the spreading dynamics. Here, the spreading and height evolution of a molten metallic droplet subjected to ultrasound of 20 kHz are investigated using high-speed imaging. The observed temporal evolution is consistent with previously reported coupling between droplet thinning, acoustic pressure, and cavitation.
